author: Bōeichō Bōei Kenshūjo Senshishitsu (War History Office, National Institute for Defense Studies, Japan Defense Agency)
title: Senshi Sōsho (戦史叢書) — War History Series
notes: Japan's official history of the war, and the thing this arc most needs and least has. It is the counterpart of Morison and the Green Books — 102 volumes compiled by the War History Office from the surviving records and from the recollections of the officers who fought — and it is essentially unreachable in English. Only three volumes have been translated: two by the Corts Foundation on the Dutch East Indies, one of which is source:remmelink-2021, and the Papua and New Britain material by the Australian War Memorial as source:bullard-2007. Nothing on Midway, Guadalcanal as a whole, the Marianas, Leyte, Iwo Jima or Okinawa exists in English from this series. Digitisation at NIDS is partial: the url above is the search system, the images are Japanese only, and a limited portion of the series is online. This entry therefore exists mainly so that citations can be honest about what stands behind them. Where the only access is an English-language author quoting a Senshi Sōsho volume, cite that author and say so in the note — never this entry, and never as though the original had been read. source:parshall-tully-2005 is the case where that chain is worth following, because they worked from the Japanese records and say which. Read the series knowing what it is: the surviving record of an army and navy that burned their classified files before the surrender, compiled by the men who had served in them. It has known silences — it does not discuss the use of chemical and biological weapons in China — and its casualty figures differ, sometimes by thousands, from those of Japan's own Ministry of Health and Welfare.
